subject: PO vs Card - procurement readiness & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Morris <janelle@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PO vs Card - procurement readiness & next steps

Hi Janelle - thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

Recap:
- Acme is evaluating Redwood to serve inference for your customer support summarization pipeline (prod target: ~2M tokens/month).
- Primary procurement path: AP team prefers Purchase Orders (POs); card payments possible for pilot but AP has vendor onboarding for production.
- Key legal/compliance asks: standard SOW, W-9, and certificate of insurance (COI) for vendor onboarding.

Next steps I can drive from our side:
1) I attached our SOW template and current pricing sheet for your review.
2) If you'll share your AP contact, we can start vendor onboarding (W-9 & COI).
3) If Acme prefers marketplace procurement, we can validate that path (may shorten vendor onboarding).

Please confirm whether you want us to: (A) proceed with PO onboarding, or (B) run pilot on card while you complete vendor setup. If PO, do you have an expected PO issuance timeline?

Thanks - I'll loop in Aditya and Dev for pricing/contract details as needed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: Redwood_SOW_template.docx, Q4-pricing-sheet.pdf

From: Janelle Morris <janelle@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card - procurement readiness & next steps

Hi Marissa - great walkthrough, thanks. A few data points from our side:
- AP policy: we prefer POs for production contracts > $25k/year. Cards are acceptable for pilots under procurement threshold.
- Vendor onboarding: our procurement team requires W-9, COI, and completed vendor questionnaire (security checklist).
- Marketplace: Procurement is open to buying via our cloud marketplace (GCP Marketplace) but that requires matching SKUs/pricing - might be faster if Redwood is available there.

Can you send W-9 and COI now? Also, our procurement lead wants to know if Redwood can accept Net 45 or if you require Net 30.

Thanks - I'll introduce you to our AP contact in the next email.

 - Janelle
Head of Product Operations
Acme Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Morris <janelle@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@acme-analytics.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card - procurement readiness & next steps

Thanks Janelle - attaching our W-9 and COI now (PDF copy) and copying Aditya (sales manager) and Dev (sales ops) to help with commercial terms.

Quick answers:
- We typically accept Net 30 for self-serve/hosted contracts; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can be flexible (Net 45 considered on enterprise deals with approved credit and an executed Master Services Agreement).
- We support card for initial pilots; for production PO is very common and we'll work with your AP to complete onboarding.
- Marketplace procurement is an option - if Acme prefers that route we can confirm SKU/pricing with our partnerships team and share a marketplace quote.

Proposed immediate items:
1) Aditya to confirm whether RDW-1427 pricing can be held for 30 days if you choose PO issuance.
2) Dev to share vendor onboarding packet (security questionnaire link + contact).
3) Janelle to introduce AP contact; we'll start vendor onboarding in parallel with legal review.

If you want, I can also set a 30-minute call between your AP and our sales ops to walk through the onboarding steps.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: W-9_Redwood.pdf

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 08:50:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Acme - PO vs Card / Net terms / onboarding

Aditya / Dev - quick internal note on Acme (RDW-1427):
- They prefer PO for production (> $25k/year). Pilot could be on card.
- They asked if we can accept Net 45. My read: standard is Net 30 but we can escalate larger deals. Can we get confirmation on Net 45 for Dedicated deals and whether finance needs an approved credit app?
- Dev: please share the vendor onboarding packet + security questionnaire link. Also confirm whether we have a signed COI template that matches their requirements (I attached our standard COI).

I'll wait for your guidance before proposing final timelines. If finance needs approvals for Net 45, we should flag this early so procurement doesn't stall.

Thanks - Marissa

From: Janelle Morris <janelle@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Hector Alvarez <hector.alvarez@acme-analytics.com>, Accounts.Payable <ap@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Mar 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PO vs Card - procurement readiness & next steps

Marissa - thanks for the fast follow-up and the docs. Introducing our AP contact:

Lindsey Park (ap@acme-analytics.com) - she'll own vendor setup and PO issuance. Lindsey, Redwood is the vendor; they can accept card for a pilot but we will move to PO for production. I've attached our vendor onboarding checklist (see inline).

From AP: expected timeline for PO issuance is ~2 weeks after vendor packet is complete and legal sign-off. Net terms: AP prefers Net 45 for new vendors; finance can make exceptions if requested.

Action items:
- Marissa: confirm if Redwood needs a credit application or any additional finance docs for Net 45.
- Lindsey/AP: confirm the exact COI limits and preferred W-9 format - I attached the checklist.

Appreciate the coordination - happy to hop on a short call if that helps move things faster.

 - Janelle
